---
title: "6A. Within-sample diversity (track A: marine plankton)"
format:
  html:
    toc: false
---

*Examine diversity **within** each sample — alpha diversity — using the [Shannon index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diversity_index#Shannon_index){target="_blank"}, and how it varies with salinity.*

### Subsample to a common depth

Samples with more reads may reveal more rare taxa, affecting diversity estimates. We therefore randomly subsample each to the same number of reads (*rarefaction*). We reuse `asv_table` from [step 5](plankton-05-beta.qmd).

First, inspect the sequencing depth (total reads) of the samples:

```r
depth <- rowSums(asv_table)
summary(depth)
sort(depth)[1:10]  # the shallowest samples
```

One sample has only 20 reads, and a few others have fewer than 10,000. Rarefying to the minimum depth would discard almost all information, so we choose 10,000 reads instead, and leave out the samples with fewer reads. These samples will have no Shannon value.

```r
set.seed(1)
asv_rarefied <- rrarefy(asv_table[depth >= 10000, ], 10000)
```

`set.seed()` makes the random subsampling reproducible.

### Calculate Shannon diversity

The Shannon index measures both the number of ASVs and how evenly their abundances are distributed. Higher values indicate greater within-sample diversity.

```r
shannon <- diversity(asv_rarefied, "shannon")
events$shannon <- shannon[events$eventID]
```

### Plot Shannon diversity against salinity

```r
plot_shannon <- function() {
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
  plot(events$salinity, events$shannon,
       pch = dataset_pch[events$dataset], bg = color_yday[events$yday],
       xlab = "Salinity", ylab = "Shannon diversity")
  legend("bottomright", bty = "n", pch = dataset_pch, legend = names(dataset_pch))
}

plot_shannon()
```

Shannon diversity shows no clear trend with salinity. Instead, it appears to vary more with season, with winter samples (blue) generally showing higher diversity than summer samples.

This complements the PCoA results in step 5: salinity is associated with differences in **which bacteria are present** (beta diversity), but not with a simple change in **within-sample diversity** (alpha diversity).

**Consider:** How can salinity be associated with community composition without showing a clear relationship with Shannon diversity?
